sources.citation: Bickford, J. Albert, Elizabeth D. Merrill, Shelley Dufoe & Alma I. Trujillo T. 2021. Language use among deaf and hearing people in a Mexican Zapotec community. Presentation, Texas Linguistic Society 2021 (online, University of Texas), 5 March 2021, 20 slides. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 88527.
sources.note: Nothing. All 20 slides read: sociolinguistic overview only (location, 2-4% deaf incidence, shared-signing-community typology, domains of use, vigesimal numerals, integration of deaf people). No phonology, prosody, accent or stress anywhere. The SIL file link is Cloudflare-blocked; the copy was fetched sources from the Wayback Machine snapshot of 2024-04-23.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2021. Change Request Number 2021-031: create [lsc] Albarradas Sign Language (adopted 2022-01-20). Submitted by J. A. Bickford, S. Dufoe, E. D. Merrill, I. Trujillo. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Identification only: shared sign language of Santa Catarina Albarradas and San Antonio Albarradas, at least 150 years old, distinct from LSM; cites Bickford et al. 2021 as the only published source.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2021. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: lsc, Lengua de señas Albarradas (associated with CR 2021-031). 4 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. States under 4(a): "Nothing published. A couple of research videos." Classifies the language as an isolate (shared sign language), 10-15 deaf signers plus a hearing population of 250-500.
